note: Input size is set from the fuzz target. The input contains embedded null bytes and ends with a newline, making doc_ends_with_newline true.
The input ends with a newline, so doc_ends_with_newline is set to true. This enables the strcspn-based line scanning path.
md_analyze_line is called for each line in the document. The input contains embedded null bytes which will be encountered during line scanning.

strcspn reads from the input buffer looking for \r, \n, or null terminator. With embedded null bytes, strcspn stops at the first null byte. When off reaches ctx->size, strcspn reads past the buffer looking for a null terminator or newline, causing a buffer over-read.
invariant: strcspn must not read past the input buffer boundary

note: After strcspn returns, CH(off) reads ctx->text[off]. If off >= ctx->size, this reads out of bounds. The embedded null bytes in the input cause strcspn to stop early, and the subsequent CH(off) check reads past the buffer.
